answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity key to be born through distributed key generation: several independent operators each hold one share, and no single party ever sees the whole key. One farmer cannot mint fifty identities alone, because each birth needs fresh co-signers staking their own standing, and keys sharing one co-signer set collapse to a single voice — like jade cut from one stone, a delta splitting into many mouths, or a cipher with only one true key.
